feature: HTTP MCP token enforcement, loopback binding, and stdio compatibility

environment.transport: production mcpServerCommand in isolated child processes

initialConditions.project: temporary disposable initialized two-shot project; snapshots use relative paths and SHA-256 content digests
initialConditions.credentials: synthetic test-only token supplied through child environment; token value omitted from this artifact
initialConditions.network: HTTP cases connect only to 127.0.0.1; no external service or production target

actions: Attempt HTTP startup with FILMBUFF_MCP_TOKEN unset, empty, and whitespace-only.
Start HTTP with a synthetic token and port 0; verify the reported bind address is 127.0.0.1.
Initialize an authenticated MCP session, then send initialize, tools/list, status, and mutating video_init requests with missing, incorrect, malformed, and wrong-scheme authorization.
Compare the disposable project snapshot after unauthorized requests and authenticated status.
Reserve a loopback port to induce EADDRINUSE and inspect sanitized startup failure.
Exercise shutdown cleanup failures with synthetic errors and inspect sanitized diagnostics.
Run stdio initialize, tools/list, and status with no HTTP token configured.

assertions.name: HTTP refuses unset, empty, and whitespace-only server tokens before writes
HTTP binds to 127.0.0.1 on the kernel-assigned port
Initialize, tools/list, status, and mutating tool calls reject missing or invalid credentials with 401 before MCP handling
Unauthorized requests leave the disposable project file snapshot unchanged
The configured Bearer token can initialize a session, list all ten tools, and call status
Bind and shutdown failures are sanitized and do not expose token values
stdio initializes, lists all ten tools, and returns status without an HTTP token
